title: Certifying Priority in Evidence-Based Allocation
abstract: arXiv:2609.21335v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Many allocation rules give priority to applicants satisfying favored conditions, including disability, homelessness, and veteran status. Because these conditions are not directly observed, a rule ranking applicants by characteristics must first determine what submitted certificates prove. This paper studies allocation with hard but partial evidence: a disability document may prove disability without proving the absence of a disqualifying tenancy record. A claim is certifiable exactly when every intended claimant has a feasible certificate excluding all outsiders. Chain rules---scores, lexicographic orders, and scalar rankings---require certification of every priority cutoff, whereas reserve rules require certification of each eligibility class. Allocation rules thus select the claim family to be certified. When certification fails, canonical repairs demote unsupported chain priorities and delete unsupported reserve labels. Nonempty reser

translated_title: 基于证据的分配中的优先权认证
translated_abstract: 许多分配规则会给予满足受优待条件的申请人优先权，这些条件包括残疾、无家可归和退伍军人身份。由于这些条件无法被直接观察，按特征对申请人进行排序的规则必须首先确定所提交的证明究竟能证明什么。本文研究了基于硬性但不完整证据的分配问题：例如一份残疾证明可以证明残疾状态，却无法证明申请人不存在被取消资格的租约记录。当且仅当每一位预期申请人都能提供可行的证明文件以排除所有外部人时，其权利主张才是可认证的。链式规则——包括分数、字典序和标量排名——需要对每一个优先级门槛进行认证，而储备规则则需要对每一个资格类别进行认证。因此，分配规则实质上决定了需要认证的权利主张族。当认证失败时，规范化修复方法会降级缺乏依据支持的链式优先级，并删除缺乏依据支持的储备标签。
tldr: 本文研究了基于不完整证据的分配中的优先权可认证性问题，证明链式规则需对每个优先级门槛进行认证而储备规则只需对每个资格类别进行认证，并在认证失败时提出了降级优先级和删除标签的规范化修复方法。
en_tdlr: This paper studies certifiability of priority in allocation with hard but partial evidence, showing that chain rules require certification of every priority cutoff while reserve rules require certification of each eligibility class, and proposes canonical repairs that demote unsupported priorities and delete unsupported labels when certification fails.
